thread_analysis.thread_summary: Hosiden wearable smartwatch registration with a SoC registered as Controller Subsystem + custom Host Stack. Four issues surfaced: (1) Controller Subsystem + incompatible Host Stack causes GAP-LL inter-layer Consistency Check failure — Combine unmodified Designs is a fallback; (2) Core-Controller DN strategy (module vendor registers Core-Controller DN, set maker includes 'use unchanged') avoids the inconsistency; (3) Q30 QDID prefix is QPRDv3.0 format and legally equivalent to old QDIDs; Combine unmodified Designs only auto-assigns DN when ≥2 QDIDs; (4) RF PHY test scope for BLE 1M-only product = 1M test only; Combine unmodified Designs cannot expand ICS.
all_questions_found: Can a Controller Subsystem QDID be combined with our custom Host Stack for Core Complete registration?
How does the Core-Controller DN strategy work to avoid GAP-LL inconsistency?
What does Q30 QDID prefix mean, and when does Combine unmodified Designs produce a DN?
What is the RF PHY test scope for a BLE 1M-only product? Can Combine unmodified Designs expand ICS to add 2M PHY later?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Post-July 2024 QPRDv3.0 Consistency Check enforces inter-layer validation. Controller Subsystem + Host Stack with conflicting GAP/LL ICS → Invalid. Core-Controller DN strategy bypasses this by having the module vendor lock the controller portion with 'use unchanged.' Q30 is simply the new QDID format number — identical legal status to old QDIDs. Combine unmodified Designs: ≥2 QDIDs → Q30 DN auto-assigned; 1 QDID → no DN. RF PHY test scope = product's actual implemented PHY modes only.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: 1. Verify QDID registration type before planning a registration strategy. 2. If Controller-only QDID + Host Stack → use Core-Controller DN strategy or Combine unmodified Designs. 3. RF PHY test = scope to actual PHY modes. 4. Combine unmodified Designs cannot add ICS — new Design required to expand scope.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Attempting incompatible Host+Controller combination generates unresolvable Consistency Check errors. Misunderstanding Combine unmodified Designs as allowing ICS expansion leads to scope mismatches at product release.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: Assuming any QDID can be freely combined with any Host Stack without verifying the ICS inter-layer compatibility under QPRDv3.0 Consistency Check rules.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For any wearable or set product using a third-party SoC QDID: check whether it is Controller Subsystem only or Core-Complete before advising a registration strategy. The Core-Controller DN strategy through the module vendor is the safest path to a real Core Complete DN.
